description: What setting this folder up involves, and how far through it you are. Setup is deliberately resumable — it takes longer than one sitting and a half-finished folder that looks finished is worse than an empty one. This file is the state: pause whenever, come back, pick up here.

columns.name: key
columns.note: Stable machine name. setup_status.py matches evidence checks on this, so don't rename one.

columns.name: phase
columns.note: Groups the dashboard. Foundation must finish before anything downstream is meaningful.

columns.name: step
columns.note: What this is, in the user's words. Shown as the row label.

columns.name: why
columns.note: One line on what breaks without it. A checklist item with no stated reason gets skipped, and one skipped item teaches people to skim the rest.

columns.name: module
columns.note: Which module this belongs to; blank for core steps. Rows for modules that aren't enabled are never created.

columns.name: required
columns.note: Needed for a working minimum. The percentage on the dashboard is computed over these; optional steps show separately so an ambitious checklist doesn't make a usable folder look unfinished.

columns.name: evidence
columns.note: DERIVED: what proves this is done — the file that exists, the row count, the config key found. Setup marks steps complete from evidence rather than from memory of having done them, because a session that crashed mid-phase remembers nothing.

columns.name: verified_date
columns.note: DERIVED: when the evidence was last confirmed against the folder.

columns.name: blocked_reason
columns.note: Why it can't proceed — a connector not authorised, a document the user has to find. Blocked is an honest state and should be used rather than leaving something Not started forever.

columns.name: notes
columns.note: Decisions taken and things deliberately deferred. This is what a later session reads to avoid re-asking a question already answered.
